entities.summary: The Codex Azcatitlan is an Aztec codex detailing the history of the Mexica and their migration journey from Aztlán to the Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire. The exact date when the codex was produced is unknown, but scholars speculate it was crafted some time between the mid-16th and 17th centuries. The name of this important Mexica pictorial manuscript was suggested by its first editor, Robert H. Barlow, who erroneously interpreted the anthill on page 2 as the glyph for “Aztlán.” In the Bibliothèque nationale de France, where it is housed, it is known as Histoire mexicaine, [Manuscrit] Mexicain 59–64.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Codex Azcatitlan provides a unique window into the history of the Mexica people and their migration journey, offering insights into the pre-Columbian Americas. Its contents have been used to inform our understanding of the Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire.
